video_title_guess: How LeBron Adjusts His Game With Age

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.quote: I'm trying to push the limit, Steve, as much as possible. There are times out on the floor where you know, like, okay, you have to maybe scale back a little bit. You have to maybe, I don't want to say preserve any energy because definitely in the postseason, it's so much harder to do that. Now, you get off the ball more than you would do when you were 28, 32. I can run 10-12 straight pick and rolls and make all the plays and pretty much not be tired at the end of that or not feel worn down in the fourth quarter. That's not probably going to be beneficial to the long term of that game or even the next game, especially in the postseason, of me running 10 straight pick and rolls or me having the ball in my hands for 10-12 straight possessions. That's just not beneficial to not only myself, and then it won't be beneficial to the team. So just kind of picking your spots, understanding like when the team may need this or need that. So playing off the ball, playing on the ball, spotting up in the corner, just trying to diversify my portfolio out on the floor in order for me to have the maximum energy that I can produce still at this point in my career.
quotes.why_it_matters: LeBron James details how he strategically adapts his playstyle, including playing off-ball and diversifying his offensive roles, to manage his energy and maximize his impact for the team, especially in the postseason, as he continues to play at an elite level into his late 30s and early 40s.
